observations: The page number «95» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01: «bare Breite», in italics, completes «schein-» at the end of p. 94 (JP2 0126, L37).

L02-L04: al-Battānī's values, set as a table in two halves divided by a vertical rule, each half with its heading, «in maxima longinquitate lunae :» and «in minima longinquitate lunae :», over two columns divided by a shorter rule; the heads of the columns in smaller type. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; a heading followed by an empty cell spans the two columns of its half. «7 dig. 42′», «8 dig. 48′», also L06, L13 and L24: the abbreviation «dig.» raised.

L01-L06. Checked against al-Battānī's table of solar eclipses (Nallino II, 91): at the greatest distance of the moon the apparent latitude is 12′ 3″ for 7 digits and 9′ 20″ for 8, the minutes of incidence 28′ 34″ and 29′ 33″; at the least distance 12′ 20″ for 8 digits and 9′ 38″ for 9, the incidence 31′ 40″ and 32′ 37″; the latitudes advance by 2′ 42″ 30‴ a digit. For 10′ 10″ linear interpolation gives 7 + 113 : 162.5 = 7.695 digits, «7 dig. 42′», and 28′ 34″ + 0.695 · 59″ = 29′ 15″; 8 + 130 : 162.5 = 8.8 digits, «8 dig. 48′», and 31′ 40″ + 0.8 · 57″ = 32′ 26″. 8 dig. 48′ − 7 dig. 42′ = 1 dig. 6′; 32′ 26″ − 29′ 15″ = 3′ 11″.

L07-L13. Checked: the table of correction (Nallino II, 89) has 44′ 0″ at 120° and 46′ 45″ at 126°, so that the anomaly 125° 7′ gives 46′ 21″ by linear interpolation, the «46 1/3» of L08; «genauer 46′ 17″» answers to an anomaly of about 125° 0′. 66′ · 46′ 17″ : 60 = 50.9′, «51′»; 191″ · 46′ 17″ : 60 = 147″ = 2′ 27″; 7 dig. 42′ + 51′ = 8 dig. 33′; 29′ 15″ + 2′ 27″ = 31′ 42″.

L14-L16. Checked: 31′ 42″ : 34′ 34″ = 0.917 hours, 55.0 minutes, «c. 55m». The hourly motion 34′ 34″ is the moon's own (al-Khwārizmī's Table 63, p. 93, JP2 0125, L27). Al-Battānī's rule (Nallino I, 111) divides the minutes of incidence «per praecessionem Lunae [respectu Solis]», by the moon's motion in excess of the sun's; with the sun's hourly motion of 2′ 31″ (Nallino II, 88) that divisor is 32′ 3″, the quotient 59 minutes, and the beginning and end 4h 12m and 6h 10m.

L17-L25. Checked: the true conjunction 18h 44m 29s (p. 83, JP2 0115); 18h 44m 29s − 1h 33m 30s = 17h 10m 59s, «rund 17h 11m», counted from the noon of 22 January, 5h 11m in the morning of 23 January; 5h 11m − 55m = 4h 16m; 5h 11m + 55m = 6h 6m; 8 dig. 33′ : 12 dig. = 0.71, «etwas mehr als 2/3». The subtraction agrees with the apparent place of the moon, 54′ ahead of its true place (p. 93, JP2 0125, L31-L33): in appearance the moon met the sun 1h 33½m, the time of 54′ of its motion, before the true conjunction.

L26-L33 and N01-N03. Checked: Meeus's algorithm (Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 54) gives a central eclipse of the sun (γ = 0.972) at the new moon of 23 January 901, its greatest phase at 7.54h Terrestrial Time, 6.93h universal time with ΔT about 0.61h, 6h 37m Cordova mean time. With the sun at 303° 20′ (declination 19° 31′ south) and the latitude of Cordova 37° 53′, the sun rose there at about 6h 59m apparent time, «erst um 7h». The local times from Oppolzer's canon for Cordova are not recomputed here.

L34-L36 and N04. Checked against Nallino I, 56: «3 2/3 horis aequinoctialibus fere ante meridiem XXIII diei mensis kānūn posterioris», 3h 40m before the noon of 23 January 901, at Antioch; Nallino converts this to 22 January, 20h 20m in the astronomical reckoning, or 23 January, 8h 20m in the morning.

L05: «der entsprechende Werte»; see the critical note. L08: «46 1/3 ∶ 60», the colon of the ratio with a space on either side (17-18 px), written ∶ (U+2236); «46 1/3» and «2/3» (L24): the fractions small, the numerator raised. L12: «(= pro spatio longinquo)», the sign of equality upright. L20: the comma after «Konjunktion» upright.
The dashes: L22 «5h 11m — 55m», the minus a long dash (42 px) with a space on either side; N04 «56—57», the long dash of the small type (37 px), set close.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Oppolzers», «Broger», «Nallino»; italics: «bare Breite», «Tabula correctionis», «maxima longinquitas lunae», «pro spatio longinquo», «quantitas incidentiae», «casus», «scheinbaren Konjunktion», «Mitte» (L20; upright in L30 and L35), «Beginn», «Ende», «Maximum», «Antiochia», «Cordova» (N01; upright in the text).
The colons, semicolons and the exclamation mark stand after the thin space of the edition (9-15 px measured).
